text:
Step-1:  Which reagent, A, gives the product?

• 8,8-Diiodobicyclo[4.2.0]octan-7-one is formed when an alkene (here cyclohexene, 6 C-atoms) undergoes a [2 + 2] cycloaddition with a dihaloketene, adding a two-carbon CO unit that carries the two halogens geminally.
• 2,2-Dihalo-ethen-1-ones (dihaloketenes) are the classic reagents for this transformation (e.g. dichloroketene + cyclohexene → 8,8-dichlorobicyclo[4.2.0]octan-7-one).
• 4,4-Diiodocyclobut-2-en-1-one is already a four-membered ring and would not give the observed product with cyclohexene.

Therefore A must be 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one.

Step-2:  Relative reactivity of the dienes (B)

The major factors governing diene reactivity (e.g. in Diels–Alder type reactions) are

1. Ability to adopt/possess the s-cis conformation (cyclopentadiene is locked s-cis and is extremely reactive).
2. Electron-donating substituents raise the HOMO and increase reactivity, but steric hindrance that disfavors the required s-cis conformation lowers it.
3. A trans (E,E) acyclic diene must undergo an energetically costly rotation to reach s-cis; a (Z,Z) diene suffers even more steric crowding in the s-cis form.

Applying these ideas:

• 3. Cyclopenta-1,3-diene  – locked s-cis → highest reactivity.
• 1. 2,3-Dimethylbuta-1,3-diene – already fairly biased toward s-cis and activated by two Me groups → next most reactive.
• 2. (2E,4E)-hexa-2,4-diene – acyclic, must rotate to s-cis; no activating groups → less reactive.
• 4. (2Z,4Z)-hexa-2,4-diene – rotation gives severe steric clash (both terminal Me groups on same side) → least reactive.

Hence the descending order of reactivity is 3  >  1  >  2  >  4.

Step-3:  Choose the option matching both conclusions

Only option (C) lists
A = 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one and
B = 3, 1, 2, 4.

Answer: C
